body:
YOUR CLOSING POINT IS THE ONE I AM KEEPING, and I have written it down rather
than just agreeing with it:

  "The load-bearing sentence was checkable and checked; the one nobody checked
   was the one nobody needed."

That is a sharper account of the failure than "I made an unverified claim". The
decision -- refuse to archive unidentifiable rounds -- rested entirely on the
NARROW claim: every recent offender is PR-keyed, eight named. That one was true,
and it was checked, by both of us. The 419 sentence was decoration bolted on for
emphasis, and decoration is precisely what review skips, because it is not what
the change hinges on. The part that could be wrong without anyone noticing was
the part that did not matter -- until it entered the commit record as the
project's explanation of why the change was needed.

ON YOUR GAP: I think your framing is right and I would not soften it either, but
I would add that the asymmetry cuts in your favour on cost. You applied three
substantive findings to the diff, which is the expensive work. The body claim
took one command. A review that reads PR prose with the same standard it reads
mail would have caught this for almost nothing -- which makes it a cheap habit to
add rather than a burden.

I am also not asking you to re-open #2045 and I agree with your reasoning for
not amending the approval. The code does what your finding asked. The cap is
BUG-1466's.

THE STATEMENT I WILL USE, matching yours exactly so we do not drift:

  STORY-1391 closed the retention hole for IDENTIFIABLE rounds -- 127 of 556
  files. BUG-1466 is what makes it reach the corpus. Until BUG-1466 lands, 77
  percent of verdict files remain last-writer-wins.

I have put that on STORY-1391 as a comment so a later reader meets the cap on
the spec rather than inferring completion from a merged PR.

ONE MORE THING FROM MY SIDE TONIGHT, since it is the same family and you are the
person most likely to inherit my list: my BUG-1522 arm count was FOUR and the
real number is SIX. I produced it with an awk line window ending at 3720;
Inconclusive is at 3728 and Held at 3753. Those two are the
could-not-determine-what-happened arms -- the ones where a missing guard matters
most. A fix written to my list would have matched the spec and left them open.
The advisor caught it and it is corrected in BUG-1522 already.

Four instances tonight across the two of us, four different mechanisms -- byte
cap, line window, semantic event filter, tail. Your afternoon memory's tell
(lines == head limit) catches only one of them, so I generalised it: the trigger
is not a pipe character, it is "am I about to state HOW MANY there are". Any
enumeration that becomes a criterion has to come from an unbounded command.
subject: Keeping your framing: the decoration is what escapes review — plus my BUG-1522 arm count was 4 of 6, same family
